# GitHub Copilot model-card catalog

<!-- Generated by models/generate.py from models/catalog.json. Edit the catalog, then run `python3 generate.py --write`. -->

> [!WARNING]
> **Not a GitHub product; provided as is, without warranty, at your own risk.** The models listed here do not necessarily match what GitHub Copilot serves now or later; consult GitHub's [supported AI models reference](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models) for the authoritative list. Publisher documents and their transcriptions remain the property of their respective owners. See the [repository README](../README.md) for the full disclaimer.

Checked **2026-10-06**. One folder per model that the GitHub Copilot CLI or the GitHub Copilot app offers, plus a utility model and recently retired models, each mapped to the most specific system card or model card from the model's publisher.

## Coverage

- **42 model folders:** 28 current, 1 limited, 1 utility-only, 12 retired.
- **35 publisher documents:** 34 PDFs (3,155 pages) and 1 Markdown model card. 40 folders map to a document; 2 have no publisher card.
- **Full text in this repository:** 2 documents whose publisher license permits redistribution. The other 33 are linked with SHA-256 provenance and can be downloaded and extracted locally; see [RIGHTS.md](RIGHTS.md).
- **Digests:** every folder has an original `digest.md` and `digest.json`, citing PDF pages (section headings for the Markdown card; owner pages for folders without a card).

## How the roster was established

- **Copilot CLI:** the `cli` column of GitHub's [per-client table](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models#supported-ai-models-per-client) (https://github.com/github/docs/blob/8f330f19fad8c83c79e7c303466fa0bc1a229e6e/data/tables/copilot/model-supported-clients.yml). 28 current or limited models are rows with CLI support; 1 more (GPT-6.1 Sol) is listed only in the CLI column of the Auto model selection table.
- **Copilot app:** the per-client table has no app column, so the app's model picker was observed on 2026-10-06: 24 of these models were listed. GitHub's [Auto selection table](https://github.com/github/docs/blob/8f330f19fad8c83c79e7c303466fa0bc1a229e6e/data/tables/copilot/auto-model-selection.yml) lists 15 as eligible for app Auto selection. Auto itself is a selector, not a model, and has no folder.
- **Release status and retirements:** GitHub's release-status table and [retirement history](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models#model-retirement-history). Retired models link to the last github/docs revision that listed them.
- **Revision:** github/docs [`8f330f1`](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/8f330f19fad8c83c79e7c303466fa0bc1a229e6e); the model tables last changed in [`dd7e864`](https://github.com/github/docs/commit/dd7e864b020676895e9e45774b0d24a231f105bc).
- Official sources only: GitHub documentation and changelog, and each publisher's own site.

## Document scope and gaps

31 folders map to a publisher document titled for that model. The others, and dedicated cards with a notable caveat, are listed here. Each folder's `source.md` records the pages and terms that establish scope.

**No publisher card**

- [GPT-5.4 nano](gpt-5.4-nano/source.md): No dedicated card. Closest owner documentation: OpenAI's [GPT-5.4 nano model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5.4-nano) (snapshot gpt-5.4-nano-2026-03-17).
- [Raptor mini](raptor-mini/source.md): No dedicated card. Closest owner documentation: GitHub's [Raptor mini public preview changelog](https://github.blog/changelog/2025-11-10-raptor-mini-is-rolling-out-in-public-preview-for-github-copilot/); GitHub's docs listed the provider as a fine-tuned GPT-5 mini. See the gpt-5-mini folder for the base model's card.

**Covered by a family or shared card (title does not name the model)**

- [GPT-5 mini](gpt-5-mini/source.md): The GPT-5 System Card covers the GPT-5 family. It states that the API provides the thinking model, its mini version, and a nano version, and reports the mini model as gpt-5-thinking-mini. No dedicated GPT-5 mini card exists. OpenAI's [GPT-5 mini model page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-5-mini) (snapshot gpt-5-mini-2025-08-07) identifies the API model; the family card's statement that the API serves the mini version of the thinking model ties GPT-5 mini to the gpt-5-thinking-mini results.
- [GPT-5.4 mini](gpt-5.4-mini/source.md): Section 6, "Appendix: GPT-5.4 mini" (PDF pages 32-36) of the GPT-5.4 Thinking System Card. No standalone GPT-5.4 mini card exists; the GPT-5.4 Thinking card devotes an appendix to it.
- [GPT-5.6 Luna](gpt-5.6-luna/source.md): The GPT-5.6 System Card covers the Sol, Terra, and Luna family members. The August update covers refreshed ChatGPT versions of Sol and Luna. The August update states that Codex and ChatGPT Work continue to use the previously released GPT-5.6 versions; GitHub does not state which GPT-5.6 Luna checkpoint Copilot serves.
- [GPT-5.6 Sol](gpt-5.6-sol/source.md): The GPT-5.6 System Card covers the Sol, Terra, and Luna family members. The August update covers refreshed ChatGPT versions of Sol and Luna. The August update states that Codex and ChatGPT Work continue to use the previously released GPT-5.6 versions; GitHub does not state which GPT-5.6 Sol checkpoint Copilot serves.
- [GPT-5.6 Terra](gpt-5.6-terra/source.md): The GPT-5.6 System Card covers the Sol, Terra, and Luna family members. The August update does not cover Terra.
- [GPT-6 Luna](gpt-6-luna/source.md): Appendix A, "GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna", of the GPT-6 Astra System Card (begins on PDF page 119). No standalone GPT-6 Luna card exists; the GPT-6 Astra card covers it in Appendix A.
- [GPT-6 Sol](gpt-6-sol/source.md): Appendix A, "GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna", of the GPT-6 Astra System Card (begins on PDF page 119). No standalone GPT-6 Sol card exists; the GPT-6 Astra card covers it in Appendix A.
- [Claude Opus 4.8 (fast mode) (preview)](claude-opus-4.8-fast-mode/source.md): The Claude Opus 4.8 System Card. The card does not mention fast mode; Anthropic's fast mode documentation states that fast mode runs the same model weights with a faster inference configuration and no change to intelligence or capabilities. Anthropic's [system-card index](https://www.anthropic.com/system-cards) listed no separate fast-mode card on the check date. Scope is substantiated by Anthropic's [fast mode documentation](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/fast-mode), a research preview offering faster output on the same model.

**Owner Markdown card (no PDF published)**

- [Kimi K2.7 Code](kimi-k2.7-code/source.md): Moonshot AI publishes no PDF system card or technical report for Kimi K2.7 Code. The Hugging Face model card (Markdown) is the owner document; the older Kimi K2 and K2.5 reports are not substituted.

**Dedicated cards with caveats**

- [GPT-5.3-Codex](gpt-5.3-codex/source.md): An earlier catalog revision described this card as HTML-only; OpenAI also publishes the PDF linked here.
- [GPT-6.1 Sol](gpt-6.1-sol/source.md): GitHub's model comparison still says the card is coming soon; OpenAI publishes the addendum PDF linked here.
- [Claude Opus 4.8](claude-opus-4.8/source.md): GitHub's comparison links an earlier revision; the canonical Anthropic URL now serves the corrected revision recorded here.
- [Claude Opus 5](claude-opus-5/source.md): GitHub's comparison links an earlier 193-page revision; the canonical Anthropic URL serves the updated revision recorded here.
- [Claude Sonnet 4.6](claude-sonnet-4.6/source.md): GitHub's comparison links an earlier revision; the canonical Anthropic URL serves the updated revision recorded here.
- [Claude Sonnet 5.5](claude-sonnet-5.5/source.md): GitHub's comparison still says the card is coming soon; Anthropic publishes the dedicated card at the canonical URL.
- [Kimi K3](kimi-k3/source.md): The technical report is the most specific publisher document for Kimi K3.
- [Grok 4.5](grok-4.5/source.md): The PDF linked from GitHub's comparison served a blank one-page file on the check date; xAI's nonblank Grok 4.5 card is recorded here.

## Limited and utility entries

| Model | Provider | Lifecycle | CLI | Publisher document | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [GPT-5.4 nano](gpt-5.4-nano/digest.md) | OpenAI | Utility only (not selectable) | No | [none](gpt-5.4-nano/source.md) | GitHub's per-client table marks it unavailable in every client except the Codex extension for VS Code (Copilot Pro+), so it is not a manually selectable CLI or app model. |
| [Claude Sonnet 4.6](claude-sonnet-4.6/digest.md) | Anthropic | Limited (annual Pro/Pro+ only) | Yes | [System Card: Claude Sonnet 4.6](claude-sonnet-4.6/source.md), 135 pp. | Retired for most plans on 2026-09-01. |

GitHub's [utility models](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/reference/ai-models/supported-models#utility-models) power background features and cannot be selected in a model picker. Besides GPT-5.4 nano, GitHub names GPT-4o mini, GPT-4o, and GPT-4.1 as utility models; they are not rows in the per-client or release-status tables (GPT-4.1 appears in the retirement history as a selectable model), so they have no folders here.

## Folder layout

```text
<model>/
  digest.md        original digest with page (or section) citations
  digest.json      the same digest as structured data (schema_version 1; see DIGESTS.md)
  source.md        roster evidence, document provenance, SHA-256, rights decision (generated)
  variants.md      Copilot identifiers, app settings, shared documents, series (generated)
  system-card.pdf  publisher PDF          (committed only when licensed; otherwise local)
  system-card.md   page-marked extraction (committed only when licensed; otherwise local)
  model-card.md    owner Markdown card, when the owner publishes no PDF
  LICENSE-*.txt    publisher license text, beside licensed copies
  supplements/     local-only supplement PDFs and extractions
```

Each `system-card.md` starts with a provenance header and has one `<!-- page N of M -->` marker per PDF page. Pages where layout conversion missed text also carry the page's complete selectable text, so no selectable text is dropped. Large TeX delimiters that have no Unicode mapping in the PDF are written as the bracket or brace they draw, and the header counts them and any unmappable glyphs. Figures and text inside images are not reproduced.

## Local download and extraction

```sh
cd models
python3 -m venv .venv && . .venv/bin/activate
python3 -m pip install -r requirements-local.txt
python3 local_cards.py --all                    # every PDF, primary and supplements
python3 local_cards.py --model grok-4.7         # one folder
python3 local_cards.py --check-urls             # owner URLs still serve the cataloged files' type
```

Outputs go into each model folder and are Git-ignored unless the document's rights are `granted`. Add `--ocr` (requires Tesseract) to OCR pages without selectable text; none of the current PDFs need it. `--report report.json` records per-page conversion coverage. `--refresh` re-downloads even when a verified copy exists, and `--pdf-cache DIR` reuses previously downloaded `<sha256>.pdf` files. A SHA-256 mismatch stops the run without replacing existing files: the publisher has changed the document, so re-verify its scope and update `catalog.json` before using the new copy.

## Maintenance

1. **Roster.** Run `python3 roster_check.py` to compare the catalog with GitHub's current tables. Re-check the app model picker. Update `catalog.json`: add models, change `lifecycle`, and for retirements set `retired_on` and `last_listed_revision`. Bump `checked_at`, `docs_revision`, and `docs_tables_commit`.
2. **Documents.** Find the publisher's most specific card for each new model and verify that it names the model. Add a `documents` entry with the owner URL, title, date, bytes, pages, SHA-256, and retrieval date. `python3 local_cards.py --model <slug>` verifies all of these. Record superseded files under `other_revisions`.
3. **Rights.** Keep `rights: not-granted` unless the publisher grants redistribution in writing or by license. A granted document needs `rights_basis` and license fields, `.gitignore` negations, and the license file committed beside it.
4. **Digests.** Write `digest.md` and `digest.json` following [DIGESTS.md](DIGESTS.md), then run `python3 digest_check.py <slug>` with the local extraction present.
5. **Generate and verify.** `python3 generate.py --write`, then `python3 generate.py --check` and `python3 -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_*.py'`.
